gbm_population_evidence.quote: radiologically confirmed (MRI and/or PET with amino-acids) diagnosis of high-grade glioma
High-grade gliomas (astrocytomas CNS WHO grade 3-4, glioblastomas, etc) are the most common primary brain tumors

candidate_evidence.quote: [RADIATION] Preoperative irradiation: After enrollment patientswith radiological signs of HGG will be irradiated by pencil beam protons
Standard treatment and follow-up: Chemoradiotherapy with a scanned proton beam combined with temozolomide 75 mg/m², given at 2 Gy × 30 fractions, to commence 4-6 weeks after surgery.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Course of preoperative proton stereotactic radiotherapy (PSRT) directed at the tumor only

role_evidence.quote: Adjuvant chemotherapy with temozolomide 150-200 mg/m² on a 5/23 schedule (maintenance chemotherapy), for 12 cycles or until disease progression/unacceptable toxicity.

agents.drug_class_hint: alkylating agent, standard postoperative chemoradiotherapy backbone
arms: Patients with radiological signs of single-focal high-grade glioma

biomarkers.biomarker_other: circulating tumour DNA and tumour molecular-biological profile

source_quote.quote: To evaluate the morphological characteristics and molecular-biological profile of the tumor tissue following the surgical treatment phase. Assess circulating tumor DNA at various stages of treatment.

coder_notes: Population is 'high-grade glioma' in conditions, title and inclusion criteria; glioblastoma is named only in the detailed description, so high_grade_glioma_unspecified (excluded at S5). The investigational intervention is preoperative proton radiotherapy only; temozolomide is part of the standard postoperative chemoradiotherapy every patient receives (soc_backbone, not a registered intervention). Fluorescence-guided resection is mentioned but no agent is named, so no diagnostic agent listed.
